page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-1xCPU-4GB is a budget-oriented instance belonging to the Cloud Native server family. It is built on the KVM hypervisor and utilizes the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration consists of 1 shared vCPU mapped to a single physical core and thread, powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. This CPU features 64 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this configuration, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that this instance delivers entry-level performance. The shared CPU allocation results in a stress-ng single-core and multi-core score of 737.38, placing it in the bottom 10% of tested systems. Similarly, memory performance is constrained, with a read-only large block bandwidth of 9.03 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 7.89 GB/sec. While single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves an average score of 9.08 GB/sec, other computational tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing fall into the bottom 10% tier. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also limited, with Redis handling 1.36 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server type is positioned as a low-cost entry point, trading high-performance compute capabilities for resource density. The shared CPU model and lack of local storage make it unsuitable for intensive database workloads, large-scale data processing, or real-time applications. However, it is appropriate for lightweight, non-critical workloads such as basic static web serving, simple text processing, small-scale software testing, or running minor background utilities that do not require sustained CPU performance.
